thesis.one_sentence: The five defining properties of wavefunction collapse in quantum mechanics (instantaneous, irreversible, non-local, regime-changing, information-gaining/freedom-losing) map one-to-one onto the five defining properties of the Fall in Genesis 3, establishing a structural isomorphism rather than a mere analogy.

claims.claim: Wavefunction collapse has five key properties: instantaneous, irreversible, non-local, qualitative regime change, and information gained but freedom lost.
claims.evidence: Standard quantum mechanics description of collapse (Schrödinger evolution to Born Rule, measurement problem).
claims.assumption: The Copenhagen interpretation (or similar) of wavefunction collapse is correct and these five properties are universally accepted.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The paper asserts these five properties as definitive, but other interpretations (e.g., many-worlds, Bohmian mechanics) do not treat collapse as a real event with these properties.

claims.claim: The Fall in Genesis 3 has five corresponding properties: instantaneous (וַיִּפָּקְחוּ), irreversible (cherubim block return), non-local (both Adam and Eve affected simultaneously), regime change (from direct communion to mediated access), and knowledge gained but innocence lost.
claims.evidence: Genesis 3:7, 3:24, 3:16-19, and theological interpretation of federal headship.
claims.assumption: A literal or structural reading of Genesis 3 as a historical event with these specific properties is valid.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The paper selects five properties from the Fall narrative that match collapse, but other interpretations of the Fall (e.g., as myth, gradual process, or allegory) would not yield these exact properties.

claims.claim: The mapping is a five-property structural isomorphism, not an analogy or metaphor.
claims.evidence: All five properties map one-to-one; the paper claims 4/5 would be analogy, 5/5 is isomorphism.
claims.assumption: The concept of 'isomorphism' can be applied across domains (physics and theology) without category error.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The paper asserts isomorphism based on a qualitative match of five properties, but isomorphism in mathematics requires a bijective structure-preserving mapping; here the mapping is interpretive, not formal.

claims.claim: The isomorphism is bidirectional: physics predicts theology and theology predicts physics.
claims.evidence: Non-locality of collapse predicts both agents affected simultaneously; irreversibility of Fall predicts measurement record permanence.
claims.assumption: The directionality of prediction is meaningful and not just post-hoc fitting.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The 'predictions' are actually retroactive interpretations; the paper does not show that collapse theory independently predicted the Fall narrative before it was known.

claims.claim: The isomorphism passes separability, reducibility, constraint, and bidirectionality tests.
claims.evidence: Tests described in section 04: separability (inseparable), reducibility (5/5 properties), constraint (rules out gradual Fall), bidirectionality (both directions hold).
claims.assumption: These tests are valid and sufficient to distinguish isomorphism from analogy.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The tests are self-defined and not independently validated; they assume the very framework they are testing.

claims.claim: The Fall is not literally a quantum measurement, and Adam and Eve are not literally wavefunctions; the claim is structural.
claims.assumption: The reader can distinguish structural from literal claims.

claims.claim: The isomorphism makes falsifiable predictions about the text: if the Fall were gradual, reversible, or affected only one agent, the mapping fails.
claims.evidence: Kill conditions listed in section 05 and constraint test in section 04.
claims.assumption: The text of Genesis 3 is sufficiently unambiguous to test these conditions.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The 'falsifiability' is conditional on accepting the interpretive framework; a different reading of Genesis could avoid the kill conditions.

claims.claim: The isomorphism is at Level 3 (Structural Isomorphism) with HIGH confidence.
claims.assumption: The classification system (Level 3) is meaningful and the confidence assessment is justified.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The confidence level is asserted without external validation or peer review.

claims.claim: Understanding collapse explains why the Fall had to be instantaneous and irreversible; understanding the Fall explains why measurement destroys what it reveals.
claims.evidence: Section 03 bidirectional arrows and section 06 predictions.
claims.assumption: The explanatory direction is meaningful and not just circular.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: This is a strong claim of mutual illumination that goes beyond structural mapping into causal or explanatory territory, without evidence that one domain actually explains the other.

claims.claim: The isomorphism is not reducible to analogy because analogy maps 2-3 properties, while this maps 5/5.
claims.assumption: The threshold for analogy vs. isomorphism is correctly set at 5/5 properties.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The paper defines analogy as mapping 2-3 properties, but this is an arbitrary cutoff; many analogies can map many properties without being isomorphisms.

explicit.definition: The instantaneous, irreversible transition from superposition to eigenstate upon measurement.
Genesis 3:6-7 — the collapse event of the moral universe.
A five-property bijective map; 5/5 properties must hold.

implied.usage_implies: That the mapping is formal and not merely metaphorical, but no formal mathematical structure is provided.
That Adam's act represents all humanity, analogous to entanglement.

undefined_but_critical: same event described in a different language

assumptions.assumption: The Copenhagen interpretation (or a collapse-based interpretation) of quantum mechanics is correct.
assumptions.if_this_fails: The five properties of collapse may not be universally accepted, weakening the mapping.

assumptions.assumption: Genesis 3 can be read as a historical event with the specific properties listed (instantaneous, irreversible, etc.).
assumptions.if_this_fails: The mapping loses its target domain.

assumptions.assumption: The concept of isomorphism can be applied across physics and theology without category error.
The five properties selected are the defining properties of both collapse and the Fall, and no other properties are equally important.
assumptions.if_this_fails: The mapping is arbitrary and not exhaustive.

assumptions.assumption: The tests in section 04 (separability, reducibility, constraint, bidirectionality) are valid and sufficient to establish isomorphism.
assumptions.if_this_fails: The claim of isomorphism is unsupported.

premises: P1: Wavefunction collapse has five properties: instantaneous, irreversible, non-local, regime-changing, information-gaining/freedom-losing.
P2: The Fall (Genesis 3) has five corresponding properties: instantaneous, irreversible, non-local, regime-changing, knowledge-gaining/innocence-losing.
P3: A five-property one-to-one mapping constitutes a structural isomorphism (not analogy).
P4: The mapping passes separability, reducibility, constraint, and bidirectionality tests.
intermediate_conclusions: IC1: The five properties of collapse map one-to-one onto the five properties of the Fall.
IC2: This mapping is an isomorphism, not an analogy.
argument_structure.final_conclusion: Wavefunction collapse and the Fall are structurally isomorphic — the same event described in different languages.
argument_structure.weakest_link: The claim that a five-property qualitative match constitutes an isomorphism (P3), as this is a non-standard use of the term.
unproven_jumps: From five matching properties to 'same event' (not just structural similarity).
From qualitative mapping to bidirectional prediction (no independent evidence of prediction).

overclaim_detection.location: Throughout, but especially in the claim that the five properties are the defining properties of collapse and the Fall.
overclaim_detection.diagnosis: The paper selects five properties that match, but does not show that these are the only or most important properties of either event.

overclaim_detection.location: Section 06: 'Collapse Predicts the Fall' and 'The Fall Predicts Collapse'.
overclaim_detection.diagnosis: The paper claims bidirectional prediction, but only shows post-hoc alignment, not independent prediction.

overclaim_detection.location: Section 01: 'That is not a metaphor for collapse. That is the same event described in a different language.'
overclaim_detection.diagnosis: The paper redefines the Fall as a collapse event, then claims to have discovered that they are the same event.

overclaim_detection.location: Section 04: Tests claim to prove isomorphism.
overclaim_detection.diagnosis: The tests are textual arguments, not empirical demonstrations; they show possibility, not actual structural identity.

addressed: The Fall is not literally a quantum measurement (section 03).
Adam and Eve are not literally wavefunctions (section 03).
The mapping could be analogy (addressed by tests in section 04).
missing: Other interpretations of quantum mechanics (many-worlds, Bohmian) that do not involve collapse.
Non-literal interpretations of Genesis 3 (myth, allegory, progressive revelation).
The problem of category error: can a physical process be isomorphic to a theological event?
The lack of formal mathematical structure to support the term 'isomorphism'.
counterarguments.smartest_critic_would_say: You have selected five properties from each domain that happen to match, but you have not shown that these are the essential or defining properties of either collapse or the Fall, nor have you provided a formal mapping that would justify the term 'isomorphism' — this is a clever analogy, not a structural identity.

kill_conditions_stated: If any property of wavefunction collapse does NOT map to any property of the Fall.
If the Fall is shown to be gradual rather than instantaneous.
If the text does not support irreversibility (humans can return to Eden by own effort).
If a better physics model for the Fall exists with more mapped properties.
kill_conditions_missing: If the five properties of collapse are not universally accepted (e.g., in other interpretations).
If the Fall narrative is interpreted non-literally (e.g., as myth).
If the mapping is shown to be arbitrary (other properties could be chosen).
If the term 'isomorphism' is shown to be inapplicable across domains.

novelty.what_is_new: A five-property structural isomorphism between wavefunction collapse and the Fall of Genesis 3, claimed as an isomorphism rather than analogy.
novelty.closest_existing_work: Analogies between quantum mechanics and theology (e.g., quantum theology, process theology), but not a specific five-property isomorphism.

compression.one_sentence: The paper argues that the five defining properties of wavefunction collapse (instantaneous, irreversible, non-local, regime-changing, information-gaining/freedom-losing) map one-to-one onto the five defining properties of the Fall in Genesis 3, establishing a structural isomorphism.
compression.three_sentences: The paper identifies five properties of wavefunction collapse and five corresponding properties of the Fall in Genesis 3. It claims that because all five properties map one-to-one, the relationship is a structural isomorphism rather than a mere analogy. The paper includes self-defined tests to support the isomorphism and lists kill conditions that would falsify it.
compression.strongest_defensible_version: There is a striking five-property structural parallel between the standard description of wavefunction collapse and a particular interpretation of the Fall narrative in Genesis 3, which may be a useful heuristic or analogy.
compression.weakest_version_still_true: The paper identifies five properties of wavefunction collapse and five properties of the Fall that can be seen as corresponding, under specific interpretive assumptions.
